model: Logistic regression over six lexical comparison features
split: Disjoint generated base names, 80/20; name patterns repeat across partitions.
generation: Deterministic indexed templates; no random sampling.
limitations: No independent test set. Threshold selection and reporting reuse validation data; results are optimistic.
Synthetic name-pair labels; validation is not real identity accuracy.
Ranks spelling variants; cannot resolve aliases, establish legal identity or certify ownership.
Scores are not calibrated real-world probabilities.
A high-scoring candidate still requires analyst review and source evidence.
No neural or LLM document extraction; supported extraction patterns are explicit and deterministic.
Synthetic labels treat some legal-suffix changes as equivalent, which is not safe to assume for real legal entities.
reproduce: Run ml/train.py using scikit-learn and numpy.

threshold_selection.dataset: validation (same data used for reported metrics)
threshold_selection.objective: Maximize selected pairs subject to observed precision >= 0.98.
threshold_selection.tie_break: Choose the largest threshold among tied candidates. This is why 0.99 was selected; it is not a business-validated operating point.

baseline_protocol: All baselines use the same validation pairs. Edit threshold 0.9 is a descriptive comparator, not a tuned or independently evaluated baseline.
interpretation: Perfect validation metrics reflect easy shared synthetic templates. They do not establish real-world generalization or model superiority.
task_boundary: Evaluation labels describe generated name variants, not ownership relationships or independently verified legal identities.
